inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares, Q3 2026 10-Q EPS note (546M). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. No buybacks in FY2025 or 9M 2026 despite a $3.0B authorisation; the flat count is a modelling convention the company is funding with debt paydown rather than repurchases.
inputs.interest_income_memo: Interest income on cash equivalents was $408M in FY2025 and $351M in 9M 2026. NOT deducted from owner FCF: Amgen is a net-debt company ($40.8B), the cash is netted inside net_debt and the interest sits in Other income, net, outside EBITDA, so the flows never contain it.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash flow statement add-back: FY2025 10-K $494M; 9M 2026 10-Q $368M vs 9M 2025 $369M -> TTM $493M. Amgen publishes no combined SBC-plus-equity-award-tax figure and no separate net-share-settlement withholding line (financing 'Other' is $52M FY2025 / $202M 9M 2026 and is not disclosed as withholding), so the add-back is used as-is.
inputs.buyback_note: Zero repurchases in FY2025 and in 9M 2026 (10-Q: 'we did not repurchase shares under our stock repurchase program'). FY2024 was $200M. The 'up to $3.0B' FY2026 authorisation is unspent; authorised is not spent.
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is the trailing twelve months to 30 Sep 2026 (FY2025 + 9M 2026 - 9M 2025): revenue 38,903; GAAP operating income 12,610; impairments 63; D&A-and-other 4,482 (of which ~3.6B is acquired-intangible amortisation); SBC 493; OCF 12,035; capex 2,454. Chosen so the flows start at the same date as the net-debt and share-count anchors; using FY2025 as FY0 with FY2026 as year 1 would double-count the nine months of 2026 cash already inside the Sep-2026 balance sheet. Year 1 therefore runs Oct-2026 to Sep-2027.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:01Z regular close (Friday; valuation written Sunday 2026-11-08, no later session)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Rf 4.2% (10y UST, Nov 2026), ERP 5.0%, equity beta 0.75 (AMGN screens ~0.55-0.65 but leverage and IRA policy exposure argue for the top of the range) -> cost of equity 7.95%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.2% (Amgen senior notes), 21% shield -> 4.1% after tax. Weights at market: equity ~$251B, debt $54B -> D/V ~18%. WACC = 0.82 x 7.95 + 0.18 x 4.1 = 7.3%, rounded up to 7.5%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios; risk is charged through the scenario paths and weights, not twice.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are immaterial (<1% of revenue). Lease cost stays inside EBITDA (treatment A); lease liabilities are NOT added to debt.
inputs.da_treatment: da_pct_path is tax-deductible PP&E depreciation and ROU amortisation only (FY2025 $763M = 2.1% of revenue; Q3 2026 $233M/qtr = ~2.4% annualised), rising with the manufacturing build. Amortisation of acquired intangibles (~$3.5B/yr; 2027 scheduled $3.5B, intangibles $19.5B remaining) is EXCLUDED: it is non-cash and, because Horizon was a stock acquisition with a deferred-tax liability unwinding against it, it is not tax-deductible, so it provides no cash tax shield. The engine's 'EBIT' is therefore EBITA, and cash_tax_rate_path is calibrated on that base.
inputs.tax_calibration: Current (non-deferred) tax: FY2025 $1,986M (provision 1,265 + deferred benefit 721); 9M 2026 $2,067M (1,480 + 587). Add back the ~21% shield on net interest expense ($1,983M 9M 2026) to unlever: ~$2.48B on 9M EBITA of ~$12.65B (OpInc 9,890 + impairment 63 + amortisation ~2,700) = ~19.6%. Cash taxes PAID in FY2025 were $4.3B because the final TCJA transition-tax instalment and settlements fell in that year; those instalments ended in 2025 and are not repeatable. Base path 19.5% -> 20% as Pillar 2 and the 2036 Puerto Rico incentive expiry bite.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: operating company). Amgen is a large-cap US biopharma; the heavy Horizon-driven leverage is handled in the WACC weights and the net-debt bridge, not by a different model. LEVERED vs UNLEVERED: last_fcf (TTM owner FCF, 9,088) is the as-reported levered figure, after ~$2.6B of net interest and after FY2025's inflated cash taxes; the projected flows are unlevered (pre-interest, net debt deducted in the bridge), so year-1 projected FCF exceeds last_fcf by roughly the after-tax interest charge plus the transition-tax normalisation. Year-1 component build: revenue 40,848 x 45.0% = 18,382 adj EBITDA, less SBC 531, less depreciation 980 = EBITA 16,871, tax 19.5% = 3,290, plus depreciation, less capex 2,655, less WC 97 -> ~11.7B unlevered owner FCF; TTM levered owner FCF 9,088 + after-tax interest ~2,050 + transition-tax normalisation ~0.5-1.0B reconciles to ~11.6-12.1B. The EBITDA margin anchor (45.0%) is GAAP operating income + impairments + D&A-and-other + SBC over revenue on the TTM (45.4%); FY2025 was 43.4%, FY2024 40.5% (Horizon integration), FY2023 47.0%. IRS TRANSFER-PRICING DISPUTE (2010-2015 notices ~$10.7B incl. interest, later years open) is NOT in the bridge; balance-sheet UTB reserves are $2.9B. An adverse Tax Court outcome would be a one-off cash call of roughly $10-20/share and is listed under key risks and inside the bear narrative.

equity_bridge.item: BeOne Medicines (ex-BeiGene) 17% equity stake, after tax
equity_bridge.note: Fair value $6.9B at 2026-09-30 (10-Q Note 6, in Other noncurrent assets), less ~21% tax on the ~$4.1B embedded gain over the ~$2.8B 2020 cost. Added because its mark-to-market gains ($2.1B FY2025, $1.2B 9M 2026) sit in Other income, net, outside the EBITDA the flows are built from (matching-asset rule). Sale is capped at 5% of BeOne per rolling 12 months, so a liquidity haircut is implicit in using after-tax value.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Forward judgment anchored to FY2026 guidance ($38.9-39.7B, midpoint +6.9% on FY2025), decaying to mid-single digits as denosumab (Prolia -45%, XGEVA -47% YoY in Q3 2026), Otezla (IRA price from 2027) and Enbrel erosion offsets Repatha, EVENITY, Imdelltra, Uplizna, TEZSPIRE and biosimilar growth. Neither historical equity CAGR is usable (see warning).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGRs (-1.7% 5yr, +33.2% 3yr) diverge from revenue (7.6% / 11.8%) by far more than 30% and carry no information: Amgen ran book equity down to $3.7B through 2022 via buybacks, then rebuilt it after the 2023 Horizon acquisition. Revenue CAGRs are inflated by the Horizon consolidation (FY2024 +19%). Owner-FCF CAGRs are negative (-4.5% 5yr) versus EPS +2.9%: FY2025 FCF carried the final TCJA transition-tax instalment and elevated MariTide-capacity capex, and SBC grew faster than cash flow (owner-FCF CAGR -4.5% vs reported -3.9%).
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on the owner-FCF series: reported FCF less SBC (interest income not stripped, net-debt company). FY2020 owner FCF 9,559 -> FY2025 7,606; FY2022 8,384 -> FY2025 7,606. TTM owner FCF has recovered to 9,088 as the transition-tax drag rolled off.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 (to Sep-2027) 5%: FY2026 guidance midpoint implies +6.9% for calendar 2026 and the Q4-2026/2027 run-rate slows as Otezla's IRA price takes effect Jan-2027 and denosumab biosimilar erosion continues. Y2-Y5 3.5-4%: launches (Repatha, EVENITY, Imdelltra, Uplizna, TEZSPIRE, PAVBLU) outgrow a shrinking legacy base; MariTide, if approved 2028, contributes modestly in the base (a few $B by Y5, not a Lilly/Novo-scale franchise). Y6-Y10 fade to 2.5% as Repatha/EVENITY exclusivity ages into the 2030s.
base.margin_rationale: 45% adjusted EBITDA (GAAP op income + impairments + D&A + SBC) is the TTM level; held flat then +0.5pt as operating leverage on launches offsets the loss of very-high-margin legacy biologics revenue. Management's non-GAAP operating margin is ~47% of product sales, consistent with this.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 guided ~$2.6B (6.6% of revenue) for MariTide and biologics capacity in Ohio/North Carolina; normalises toward 3.6% (FY2024 was 3.3%) by Y8. Terminal capex 3.6% slightly above terminal depreciation 3.4%.
base.terminal_rationale: 2% perpetual growth and a 15x FCF cap: large pharma with recurring patent cliffs is a structurally slower business; 15x is the mid-point of where the sector has traded on FCF. Gordon at 7.5%/2% gives 18.5x, so the cap is expected to bind.

bull.rationale: MariTide Phase 3 (2027) delivers differentiated monthly dosing with acceptable tolerability, approval 2028, ramps to a ~$6-8B franchise by Y6-Y7 (revenue growth peaks at 9% in Y4-Y5). Repatha and EVENITY keep compounding at 20%+ for several more years, Imdelltra/Uplizna/TEZSPIRE scale, no further IRA selections hit major products. Margin to 48% on launch leverage; 18x cap for a company that has re-established a growth franchise.

bear.rationale: Denosumab (Prolia/XGEVA ~$3.5B run-rate) halves again, Otezla loses ~40% on IRA pricing from 2027, Enbrel keeps eroding, TEPEZZA and KRYSTEXXA stay flat-to-down, and a further IRA cycle selects another major product; MariTide fails to differentiate from oral GLP-1s and is shelved or launched sub-scale. Revenue flat-to-down through Y4, then 1% growth. Price erosion falls straight through to margin (40% by Y6). Cash tax 21% as the jurisdictional mix worsens and the IRS dispute settles unfavourably. 12x cap and 1% terminal growth for an ex-growth pharma; the manufacturing capex is already committed and does not flex down.

scenario_narratives.base: Amgen is a volume-led, price-eroding large pharma: FY2025 product volume +13% against -3% net price, and Q3 2026 revenue +8%. The base case assumes that pattern persists but slows: launches (Repatha +37%, EVENITY +39%, Imdelltra +128%, Uplizna +191% YoY) keep outgrowing a legacy base that is shrinking fast (Prolia -45%, XGEVA -47%, Otezla -18%, with Otezla's IRA price landing in 2027), giving ~4% growth to 2031 and 2.5% thereafter. MariTide is credited only modestly. Margins hold at ~45% adjusted EBITDA, capex normalises from the 2026 manufacturing peak, and the ~$41B of net debt plus a ~$6B after-tax BeOne stake are bridged at the Sep-2026 balance sheet. The valuation axis is simple: can newer products out-run biosimilar and IRA erosion for a decade without MariTide carrying the load.
scenario_narratives.bull: MariTide's six Phase 3 MARITIME studies read out in 2027 with differentiated monthly (or less frequent) dosing and acceptable GI tolerability; approval in 2028 and a multi-billion franchise by the early 2030s re-rates Amgen as a growth pharma. Repatha and EVENITY compound for several more years as guidelines favour earlier LDL lowering and bone-building therapy, Imdelltra/Uplizna/TEZSPIRE scale, and the bolt-on oncology pipeline (Dark Blue, DISCO) refills the late-stage shelf without re-levering. Margins expand to 48% on launch leverage and the market grants an 18x terminal multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: Legacy erosion is faster and broader than the launches can offset: denosumab halves again, Otezla takes the full IRA price cut, Enbrel continues down, TEPEZZA and KRYSTEXXA never justify the $27.8B Horizon price, and a further IRA negotiation cycle selects another major Amgen product. MariTide, years behind Lilly and Novo and facing oral GLP-1s, fails to differentiate and is shelved or launched sub-scale. Revenue stalls through 2030, price erosion compresses adjusted EBITDA margin to 40%, the IRS transfer-pricing dispute settles adversely (a one-off cash call not in these flows), and the $54B debt stack is serviced out of a flat cash flow with no room for buybacks. 12x terminal and 1% growth: an ex-growth pharma.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved off the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bull weight DOWN: the bull case needs MariTide to succeed in a market Lilly and Novo already dominate (binary Phase 3 data not before 2027, late entrant, oral competition) AND Repatha/EVENITY to keep compounding AND no further IRA selections; several independent things must go right. Bear weight UP: the legacy erosion is observable today (Prolia/XGEVA -45%/-47%, Otezla IRA 2027), IRA selection risk is a single-regulator dependency, and $54B of debt removes the buyback cushion; there is no going-concern risk (investment grade, ~$12B unlevered FCF), which is why bear is 25% and not higher.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF with SBC fully expensed and the share count held flat; unlevered flows discounted at a 7.5% USD WACC with $40.8B of Sep-2026 net debt deducted and the BeOne stake added after tax. Tax-deductible depreciation only in D&A, with the non-deductible Horizon amortisation excluded and the cash-tax rate calibrated on EBITA. Three scenarios built on Amgen's actual axes: launch growth vs biosimilar/IRA erosion, MariTide optionality, leverage. Terminal value capped at 12-18x FCF because large pharma faces recurring patent cliffs.
key_risks_to_valuation: Biosimilar erosion speed on denosumab, Enbrel and biosimilar-exposed legacy products; Q3 2026 showed -45% to -47% YoY on Prolia/XGEVA.
IRA Medicare price negotiation: Enbrel (2026) and Otezla (2027) already selected; further cycles could select Repatha, Prolia or EVENITY.
MariTide Phase 3 readouts (2027) are binary and against entrenched Lilly/Novo franchises and oral GLP-1s; the bull case depends on them.
$54B debt from the Horizon acquisition: refinancing cost sensitivity and no buyback cushion; TEPEZZA/KRYSTEXXA returns on the $27.8B price are in doubt.
IRS transfer-pricing dispute (2010-2015 ~$10.7B incl. interest; later years open) is not in the flows or the bridge; an adverse outcome is a one-off ~$10-20/share.

The 15x terminal cap binds in the base case; if the market continues to pay ~24x unlevered FCF (today's EV/FCF) the DCF will look conservative, but that is a multiple the model deliberately does not grant.
Terminal value is a large share of EV at a 7.5% WACC; the sensitivity grid shows how fast value falls at 8.5-9.5%.
